sampling.description: The percentage of matching observations that will be evaluated. Lower sampling rates reduce evaluation volume and cost.
cost.totalDescription: Sum of the available weekly LLM cost estimates for attached evaluators.
cost.noMatches: No observations matched this rule in the last 7 days, so there is nothing to estimate yet. It will evaluate matching observations as they arrive.
cost.confirm: Activating this rule may incur costs. Are you sure you want to continue?
cost.matches: {{total}} observations matched this rule in the last 7 days.
cost.sampleSingle: This evaluator would run on {{sampled}} of the {{total}} matching observations.
cost.sampleEach: Each evaluator would run on {{sampled}} of the {{total}} matching observations.
cost.unavailable: No cost estimate is available for {{total}} other LLM evaluators.
version.conflict: Another user saved a newer version while you were editing. Discard your changes to load the latest version, or override it by saving your changes as the newest version. The other version remains in the version history.
model.defaultDescription: Evaluators that follow the project default will use the new model on their next run. Evaluators with their own model are untouched. New evaluators start on the default.
sample.ruleDescription: Define which incoming observations match this rule.
sample.ruleTooltip: Only new observations matching these filters are evaluated by this rule.
sample.ruleMatches: The first match is used to preview attached evaluator mappings.
sample.ruleMatchTooltip: Observations matching the rule filters over the last seven days.
sample.evalDescription: Filter the observations to a representative sample for testing this evaluator.
sample.evalTooltip: These filters control which observations you can pick to test with.
sample.evalMatches: Select an observation to test the evaluator and verify the variable mapping.
sample.evalMatchTooltip: Observations matching the current filters and global time range.
saved.title: Evaluator saved
saved.skipHelp: It remains available for batch evaluations and prompt experiments. Set up incoming observations later.
saved.reuseDescription: Creates a rule from the sample observation filters.
saved.differentDescription: Attach to a rule you already have, or create a new one.
saved.omittedDescription: {{omitted}} of {{total}} sample filters are only used for testing and will not be included in this rule.
definition.description: Choose whether an LLM or your own code evaluates the data, then define the instructions it follows and the score it reports.
backfill.capped: {{total}} observations in {{range}} — capping at {{limit}}, newest first.
backfill.withinLimit: {{total}} observations in {{range}}, all within your limit.
test.description: Run the evaluator against the selected observation to check that it scores the way you'd expect.
rules.deleteDescription_one: This permanently deletes {{count}} rule and its evaluator assignments.
rules.deleteDescription_other: This permanently deletes {{count}} rules and their evaluator assignments.
mapping.variableDescription: Variable in the template to be replaced with the mapped data.
mapping.traceJsonPath: Optional selection: Use JsonPath syntax to select from a JSON object stored on a trace. If not selected, we will pass the entire object into the prompt.
mapping.jsonPath: Optional selection: Use JsonPath syntax to select from a JSON object. If not selected, we will pass the entire object into the prompt.
evaluator.paused: The evaluator has been used in the past but is currently paused. It will not run against outputs created in this dataset run. You can reactivate it if you wish
rules.creator: Created by {{creator}}
rules.attachDescription: Attach an evaluator to run on matching observations.
mapping.noSample: No matching observation is available to validate JSON paths.
mapping.invalid: Some variables are not mapped correctly
mapping.variables.title: Map variables to data
mapping.variables.description: Choose how observation fields populate each variable in your evaluation prompt. The live preview fills in real data so you can verify the mapping.
mapping.state.title: Build the state
mapping.state.description: Choose which observation fields the decision model sees, as one JSON object. Questions refer to these fields by name; the live preview shows the exact object sent.
steps.label: Step {{number}}: {{title}}
rules.activeDescription: This rule is active. Based on matching observations and the latest evaluator trace from the last seven days:
rules.legacyDisabled: Legacy rules cannot be re-enabled because trace- and dataset-level evaluations are deprecated. Create an observation-based rule instead.
rules.relationships_one: This evaluator is used by {{count}} rule. Attach it to a rule to run the evaluator on incoming observations.
rules.relationships_other: This evaluator is used by {{count}} rules. Attach it to a rule to run the evaluator on incoming observations.
sample.noResults: No observations match the current filters and time range.
decision.choiceSummary: Pick one of a fixed set of labels.
decision.choiceExample: Which team should handle this ticket?
decision.choiceWhen: The answer is one of a few options with no order between them. Add an “other” option if the list may not cover every input.
decision.scoreSummary: Rate along ordered levels you describe.
decision.scoreWhen: The answer sits on a spectrum you can describe in steps. Describe situations, not degrees: “broken but a workaround exists” beats “moderately severe”.
decision.yesNoSummary: Get the probability a statement is true.
decision.yesNoExample: Does the message request a refund?
decision.yesNoWhen: A clean yes/no where the probability itself is the signal. Define the condition precisely; 0.5 means undecided, not “medium”.
decision.writesChoice: Writes a categorical score with one of {{total}} labels.
decision.writesScore: Writes a numeric score from 0 to {{maximum}} (expected level; can fall between levels).
decision.writesProbability: Writes a numeric score from 0 to 1: the probability the answer is yes.
decision.typesHelp: Choice picks one of a fixed set of labels. Score rates along ordered levels you describe. Yes/no returns the probability that a statement is true. Pick the one your code can act on directly.
decision.scoreNamesHelp: Each question writes its own score under this name. Keep it stable: renaming starts a new score series.
decision.yesCriteria: The user clearly asks for money back, a refund, or a chargeback.
decision.noCriteria: A complaint or question without asking for money back.
decision.instructionsHelp: Ask for one snap judgment a knowledgeable person makes in a second. Name the state field the question is about in backticks, for example “Does `question` request a refund?”. The model reads the state as a JSON object, so the question does not repeat the data.
decision.questionsHelp: Each question is one snap judgment about the state and writes one score. All questions are answered in a single model call, so a second or tenth question costs only its own tokens.
decision.noQuestions: No questions yet. Start from an example to see the shape of each type, or add a blank question.
decision.optionsHelp: One label per option. A short description sharpens the boundary between options; add an “other” option when the list may not cover every input.
decision.lowest: Lowest level, e.g. Calm, just stating facts
decision.highest: Highest level, e.g. Very angry or threatening to leave
decision.levelsHelp: Each level is one point on the scale. The model judges every level on its own against the state and returns a position between them, so describe situations (“broken, but a workaround exists”), not degrees (“moderately severe”). Two to ten levels; drag to reorder.
decision.weightedScore: The score is the probability-weighted average of the level numbers, so it can be a decimal from 0 to {{maximum}}.
score.outputHelp: Use a number for continuous judgments like helpfulness. Use a category for explicit labels like correct or incorrect. Use a boolean for binary decisions like true or false.
score.deleteScheduled: Selected scores will be deleted. Scores are removed asynchronously and may continue to be visible for up to 15 minutes.
score.metadataHelp: Add metadata to scores to track additional information.
score.userHelp: The user ID associated with the trace.
score.evaluatorHelp: The evaluator associated with the score.
score.jobConfigHelp: The Job Configuration ID associated with the score.
score.deleteConfirmation: This action permanently deletes scores and cannot be undone. Score deletion happens asynchronously and may take up to 15 minutes.
annotation.multipleDescription: Annotate the trace and observation with scores to capture human evaluation across different dimensions.
model.connectionHelp: LLM-as-a-judge evaluations require an LLM connection for scoring. You can also specify a custom model for each evaluator.
sdk.observations: This evaluator targets observations, which require JS SDK v4+ or Python SDK v3+. You can still configure this evaluator now—it will start running once you upgrade.
sdk.runner: The Experiment Runner SDK requires JS SDK v4.4+ or Python SDK v3.9+. You can still configure this evaluator now—it will start running once you upgrade.
sdk.learnRunner: Learn more about the Experiment Runner SDK.
sdk.legacyRuns: This evaluator targets traces from legacy low-level SDK methods for dataset runs that manually linked dataset items to traces. Consider upgrading to the Experiment Runner SDK for improved performance and features.
sdk.recommendObservations: Observation evaluators provide more granular control and an easier workflow. We strongly recommend upgrading to observation evaluators.
rules.unsupportedPaused: This evaluator contains deprecated or unsupported filters. The filters must be removed. Until the filters are removed, the evaluator is paused and will not be run.
sdk.noOtel: We did not find any data ingested with langfuse OTEL-compatible SDKs in the last 7 days. Observation-level evaluators require JS SDK v4+ or Python SDK v3+. You can still configure this evaluator now—it will start running once you upgrade.
rules.legacyFilter: This evaluator has a filter that is not supported for trace-level evaluators. It is effectively paused. Please remove all filters and re-add them from scratch to resume execution.
rules.targetImmutable: An evaluator's target data may only be configured at creation.
rules.delayHelp: Time between first Trace/Dataset run event and evaluation execution to ensure all data is available
sdk.traceDeprecated: We strongly recommend using observation evaluators. Trace evaluators will be deprecated in the future. Only proceed if you are sure you cannot upgrade your SDK version now.
model.setupDefault: LLM-as-a-judge evaluators need an LLM connection for scoring. Set a project default connection now to continue defining the evaluator.
sdk.code: Code evaluators require JS SDK v4+ or Python SDK v3+. You can create this evaluator now, but it will only run once your project ingests data with a compatible SDK.
model.noDefault: No default model set. LLM-as-a-judge evaluations require an LLM connection for scoring. This default is used by all templates that don't specify their own model.
score.chooseType: Choose whether the evaluator should return a numeric score, a boolean verdict, or one of a fixed set of categories.
score.categoriesHelp: Add the allowed category values the model may return. Categories must be exhaustive. If you need a catch-all outcome (e.g. 'No match'), add it explicitly as one of the categories.
score.multipleHelp: Lets the model return more than one category. One score will be created for each selected match.
score.reasoningHelp: Define how the LLM should explain its evaluation. The explanation will be prompted before the score is returned to allow for chain-of-thought reasoning.
mapping.previewHelp: Preview of the evaluation prompt with the variables replaced with the first matched trace data subject to the filters.
rules.upgrade: Evaluators are moving to observation-level. Upgrade this configuration to keep its scores aligned with the v4 data model.
gallery.decisionHelp: Ask TypeSafe Jev typed questions about each observation and get calibrated answers in one call, at a fraction of an LLM judge's cost. Experimental.
decision.methodsHelp: Use custom code for deterministic checks like exact matches, regex, or schema validation. Use an LLM when the check needs judgment, such as rating helpfulness, tone, or answer quality. Use a decision model (experimental) for a fast, cheap label with calibrated probabilities when the possible answers are known upfront.
gallery.introduction: Evaluators score your data with an LLM-as-a-judge or with code. Run them on production traces to catch patterns, or on dataset runs to evaluate changes before you ship.
sdk.verifyRunner: Please verify you are using the Experiment Runner SDK
validation.promptContent: Add content to every prompt message before saving.
validation.systemFirst: System messages are only allowed as the first prompt message.
validation.scoreName: Every question needs a score name.
validation.minCategories: At least two categories are required.
validation.nameBeforeSaving: Add an evaluator name before saving.
validation.codeBeforeSaving: Fix the code validation errors before saving.
gallery.safetyHelp: These evaluators run after the fact on completed traces. They are not real-time guardrails.
gallery.decisionHint: Ask TypeSafe Jev typed questions and get calibrated answers in one call. Experimental.
gallery.detectTopicsDescription: Classify the requests going through your system to better understand volumes of different categories.
gallery.template.chat-intent.name: Detect Chat Intent
gallery.template.chat-intent.description: Classifies the user's primary request into one predefined intent category.
gallery.template.out-of-scope-request.de: Checks whether the user's request is clearly outside the assistant's defined role or supported scope.
gallery.template.user-disagreement.name: Detect User Disagreement
gallery.template.user-disagreement.descr: Detects whether the user perceives the assistant as making an error or heading in the wrong direction.
gallery.template.all-caps.name: Detect User Frustration (ALL CAPS)
gallery.template.all-caps.description: Detects whether user uses all capital letters, potentially indicating frustration.
gallery.template.user-distress.name: Detect User Distress
gallery.template.user-distress.descripti: Detects whether the latest user message expresses clear, meaningful emotional distress.
gallery.template.correctness.name: Check Correctness
gallery.template.correctness.description: Checks whether the actual output matches the expected output in material meaning.
gallery.template.exact-match.name: Check if Output Is an Exact Match
gallery.template.exact-match.description: Checks whether the output exactly matches the expected output.
gallery.template.keyword-match.name: Validate Keyword Overlap
gallery.template.keyword-match.descripti: Scores what fraction of expected keywords from keyword_overlap appear in the output.
gallery.template.answer-relevance.name: Check Answer Relevance
gallery.template.answer-relevance.descri: Checks whether the response actually addresses the user's question or task.
gallery.template.quality-criterion.name: Judge on One Quality Criterion
gallery.template.quality-criterion.descr: Checks whether output follows a defined quality criterion.
gallery.template.topic-classifier.name: Classify Input Topic
gallery.template.topic-classifier.descri: Assigns the input, output, or conversation to one of a predefined set of topics.
gallery.template.language-classifier.des: Classifies input into one of the pre-defined language categories.
gallery.template.answer-groundedness.des: Checks whether the output is supported by the provided context and avoids unsupported claims.
gallery.template.context-precision.name: Check Context Precision
gallery.template.context-precision.descr: Checks whether the provided context is actually useful and relevant for producing the answer.
gallery.template.context-recall.name: Check Context Recall
gallery.template.context-recall.descript: Checks whether the provided context covers the information needed to support the answer.
gallery.template.pii-leakage.name: Detect PII Leakage
gallery.template.pii-leakage.description: Checks whether assistant output contains sensitive personal information that could identify or harm a private individual.
gallery.template.rule-adherence.name: Check Rule Adherence
gallery.template.rule-adherence.descript: Checks whether the output follows a defined policy, instruction set, rubric, or formatting rule.
gallery.template.prompt-injection.name: Detect Prompt Injection
gallery.template.prompt-injection.descri: Checks whether the input contains attempts of prompt injection.
gallery.template.engineering-task-type.d: Categorizes the type of task the coding agent is used for.
gallery.template.coding-agent-department: Classify Coding Agent Usage per Department
Classifies coding-agent usage into department buckets.
gallery.template.topic-decision-model.de: Assigns the input to one of your topics with a calibrated probability for each option, in one fast decision-model call.
gallery.template.out-of-scope-decision-m: Returns the probability that the user's request falls outside what the assistant is meant to handle.
gallery.template.frustration-decision-mo: Rates how frustrated the user sounds along levels you describe, from calm to ready to leave.

onboarding.promptsDescription: Langfuse Prompt Management helps you centrally manage, version control, and collaboratively iterate on your prompts. Start using prompt management to improve your LLM application's performance and maintainability.
onboarding.datasetsDescription: Datasets in Langfuse are collections of inputs (and expected outputs) for your LLM application. You can run Experiments against these datasets to test new releases before deployment to production.
onboarding.scoresDescription: Scores allow you to evaluate the quality/safety of your LLM application through user feedback, model-based evaluations, or manual review. Scores can be used programmatically via the API and SDKs to track custom metrics.
onboarding.queuesDescription: Annotation queues help you manage manual annotation/labeling for your LLM projects. Create queues, define annotation metrics, and track progress.
onboarding.usersDescription: Once you add a user ID to your traces, you can correlate costs, evaluations and other LLM Application metrics to better understand how they interact with your LLM applications.
onboarding.sessionsDescription: Sessions let you group traces that belong to the same workflow, or conversation.
onboarding.judgeDescription: Create evaluation templates and evaluators to automatically score your traces with LLM-as-a-judge. Set up custom evaluation criteria and let AI help you measure the quality of your outputs.
onboarding.itemsDescription: Datasets are collections of specific edge cases and underrepresented patterns used to evaluate your application.
onboarding.itemsUploadHelp: Import dataset items from a CSV file
onboarding.itemsCodeHelp: Use our Python/TS/JS SDKs or custom API
onboarding.itemsObservationsHelp: Select observations in the observations table and use a batch action to add them to your dataset
onboarding.userIdHelp: To start tracking users, you need to add a userId to your traces.
onboarding.sessionIdHelp: To start using sessions, you need to add a sessionId to your traces.
onboarding.noAccess: You don't have access to this feature, please contact your administrator
onboarding.evalIntroduction: Use evaluators to score traces and observations automatically. Langfuse supports two evaluator types:
onboarding.judgeType: LLM-as-a-judge evaluators use an LLM to score outputs against natural-language criteria.
onboarding.codeType: Code evaluators use {{languages}} logic for deterministic, custom scoring.
